newsitem.title: GHANA: Ghanaian cocoa stocks seen rising at Takoradi.
newsitem.headline: Ghanaian cocoa stocks seen rising at Takoradi.

text.p: Cocoa trucks and railway wagons are queuing up to be unloaded at Ghana's second port as warehouses fill up and shipments are seen dropping, shipping agent and transporters told Reuters.
About 28 400-tonne capacity Ghana Railway Corp wagons were waiting to be unloaded at Ghana's second port, Takoradi, said a port source. Another 100 privately owned trucks were also waiting.
"The problem is organisation," said one shipping agent. "This year cocoa was moved from the hinterland to the ports much faster than last year," said a port source.
Stocks were rising in spite of higher shipment levels in late 1996 than in late 1995. Queues also built up at Takoradi in Janauary 1995 but overall shipments were smaller.

Total November and December 1996 shipments from Ghana, including the main port Tema, totalled 31,474 tonnes, according to one shipper's figures. Over the same period in 1995 about 26,737 tonnes were shipped.
Shipping sources said January 1996 figures were still unclear but one unconfirmed report said amounts were small.
Warehouse stocks were also rising at Tema, shipping agents said, without giving precise figures.
